item.title: Thursday Weather: Sunshine and warm temps - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Mary Apel
item.description:
Good morning! We’re settling into a really nice stretch of weather across Mississippi, with warm temperatures, lots of sunshine and very little chance for rain through the rest of the week.

Today will be sunny with a high around 83 degrees and light northeast winds at 5 to 10 miles per hour. Humidity stays fairly comfortable this afternoon, and rain chances are almost nonexistent at just 2 percent. Tonight will be partly cloudy and pleasant, with lows dipping to around 59 degrees.

Looking ahead, temperatures will continue to warm under mostly sunny to sunny skies. Highs will generally stay in the low to mid-80s for the next few days before some areas start pushing close to 90 degrees by late week. Overnight lows will also trend warmer heading into the weekend and into next week.

The good news is the dry pattern is expected to hold through the weekend, with the next meaningful rain chances likely holding off until early next week. So if you’ve got outdoor plans, it’s shaping up to be a great stretch of weather to enjoy.

item.title: Texas man pleads guilty in federal cocaine trafficking case tied to 19 defendants - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
GREENVILLE — A Texas man pleaded guilty Tuesday in federal court in connection with a large-scale drug trafficking investigation that resulted in the seizure of more than 25 kilograms of cocaine, approximately $150,000 in drug proceeds and multiple vehicles, according to federal officials.

Harold Cook, 55, of Fort Worth, Texas, entered the guilty plea after a federal jury had already been selected in the case, prosecutors said.

According to court documents, Cook and his co-defendants were charged in an indictment that included cocaine conspiracy, money laundering conspiracy, possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime and possession with intent to distribute cocaine.

His co-defendants include:

Cook will be sentenced later by Chief U.S. District Judge Debra M. Brown. He was remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service following his guilty plea.

Federal officials said the investigation was part of the Homeland Security Task Force initiative established in 2025 to target criminal cartels, human smuggling operations and drug trafficking organizations.

“We are all aware of the devastation that drug trafficking and violent gangs have visited on our communities,” Scott F. Leary, U.S. attorney for the Northern District of Mississippi, said in a statement. “By dismantling this drug trafficking organization, hundreds of pounds of drugs will be taken off our streets and lives will be saved.”

Leary praised the work of the DeSoto County Sheriff’s Department, along with DEA offices in Oxford, El Paso and Fairview Heights, Illinois, as well as the United States Marshals Service.

Steven Hofer, special agent in charge of the DEA, said the operation demonstrated cooperation between federal, state and local agencies.

“We are sending a clear message that criminal organizations have no place in Mississippi,” Hofer said.

The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Sam Stringfellow and Julie Addison.

item.title: STEPPING UP TO SERVE: Pure Air Consultants, Hometown Magazines provide HVAC system to young family in need - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Pure Air Consultants , a local, family-owned HVAC company, in partnership with Hometown Magazines, recently provided a new heating and cooling system to a young local family through the company’s PAC Gives Back initiative.

The recipient family is a newlywed couple, ages 21 and 22, who have taken in their nephew and are working to build a stable home for him.

Through the giveaway, the family received a new 14 SEER Day & Night heating and cooling system installed by Pure Air Consultants. The company said the initiative was created as a way to give back to the community that has supported its growth over the years.

Pure Air Consultants announced the program earlier this year, seeking nominations for individuals or families in Hinds, Madison and Rankin counties who were in need of a new heating and cooling system but could not afford to replace an old or inefficient unit.

Company representatives said the giveaway was intended to help a family facing hardship while also recognizing the importance of safe and reliable home comfort.

Pure Air Consultants partnered with Hometown Magazines to help promote the initiative and encourage nominations from across the metro Jackson area.

The company said providing the system to the selected family was a meaningful opportunity to support a household working to care for a child and create a secure home environment.

Pure Air Consultants is a locally owned and operated HVAC company that offers heating and cooling services, duct cleaning, UV lights and air purifiers.

Check out the heartwarming video that Hometown Magazine put together when they surprised the young family.

item.title: Ridgeland to host Memorial Day ceremony, America250 exhibit - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
RIDGELAND — The City of Ridgeland will host a Memorial Day ceremony and unveil a new America250 exhibit on May 21 at Ridgeland City Hall.

The public ceremony will take place at 10 a.m. in Veterans Memory Park at City Hall, located at 100 W. School St. Guests are encouraged to arrive by 9:45 a.m.

The park features memorial benches and plaques honoring the six branches of the U.S. military, along with the Walk of Heroes, a flagpole and a seven-foot bell tower.

Retired Brig. Gen. Joe Hargett will deliver keynote remarks during the ceremony. Gene McGee, mayor of Ridgeland, and Col. John McCollum are also scheduled to speak.

The program will include a presentation of colors by the Ridgeland High School AFJROTC, along with music from the National Guard Band and Dr. Catherine Sledge.

Following the ceremony, attendees will be invited to tour a new America250 exhibit curated by Nancy Batson, chair of the City History Committee.

Chaplain David Morris and members of the Ridgeland Board of Aldermen and other city officials are also expected to participate.

item.title: Mississippi Museum of Natural Science named Best Museum in Mississippi - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON – The Mississippi Museum of Natural Science has been named Best Museum in Mississippi in Mississippi Magazine’s Best of Mississippi 2026 Reader Poll, officials announced this week.

The annual poll recognizes businesses, attractions and destinations across the state, with winners selected by readers of Mississippi Magazine.

Located inside LeFleur’s Bluff State Park in Jackson, the museum features interactive exhibits, aquariums, native wildlife displays, educational programming and nature trails focused on Mississippi’s natural heritage.

“We are honored to receive this recognition,” Museum Director Angel Rohnke said in a statement. “This award reflects the dedication of our staff and the support of the visitors and communities we serve.”

Officials said the museum offers educational and interactive experiences for visitors of all ages throughout the year.

The museum is located at 2148 Riverside Drive in Jackson. Admission is $9 for adults, $7 for youth ages 3 to 18 and $8 for seniors ages 60 and older.

More information is available through the Mississippi Museum of Natural Science website.

item.title: Mexican national sentenced to more than 10 years in child exploitation case in Mississippi - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
ABERDEEN — A Mexican national living illegally in the United States has been sentenced to more than 10 years in federal prison after pleading guilty to distributing and receiving child sexual abuse material through Facebook Messenger, federal officials announced.

Adolfo Raul Vasquez-Santana, 32, of Southaven, was sentenced to 121 months in prison, followed by five years of supervised release. Senior U.S. District Judge Sharion Aycock also ordered him to pay $14,000 in restitution to victims.

According to court documents, Vasquez-Santana downloaded and shared violent videos depicting the sexual abuse of children through the messaging platform Facebook Messenger.

The investigation began after the Southaven Police Department received a tip from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children. Homeland Security Investigations later determined Vasquez-Santana was in the country illegally and pursued federal charges.

Officials with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement have placed an immigration detainer on Vasquez-Santana, meaning he is expected to be removed from the United States after serving his federal sentence.

“Child pornography is a plague,” Scott F. Leary, U.S. attorney for the Northern District of Mississippi, said in a statement. “Children are victimized not only through the production of obscene material, but through its continual distribution.”

Leary also praised the work of Southaven police, Homeland Security Investigations and Assistant U.S. Attorney Julie Addison, who prosecuted the case.

Matt Wright, acting special agent in charge for HSI New Orleans, said investigators acted quickly after receiving information about the defendant.

“HSI is committed to protecting children from predators who use technology to exploit them,” Wright said. “We remain vigilant against child predators and will continue to pursue these offenders wherever they operate.”

Federal officials said the case was part of both Operation Take Back America and Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide Department of Justice initiative aimed at combating online child sexual exploitation.

item.title: McComb man arrested in Vicksburg on child sex crime charges - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PIKE COUNTY – A McComb man was arrested Wednesday morning in Vicksburg on child sex crime charges.

The Pike County Sheriff’s Office said Sheriff Wally Jones, along with Pike County investigators and deputies and investigators from the Warren County Sheriff’s Office, arrested Christopher Scott Landrum around 7 a.m. May 13.

Landrum was charged with one count of sexual battery and one count of enticing a minor child, according to the sheriff’s office.

Jones said his office will continue pursuing people accused of targeting children in Pike County, no matter where they are located.

“I’ve been very clear to anybody who has criminal intentions in Pike County, especially those who target children — you do not have a safe haven in Pike County,” Jones said.

Jones thanked Pike County investigators and the Warren County Sheriff’s Office for their help in the case.

The sheriff’s office is asking any additional victims related to the case to come forward and contact the Pike County Sheriff’s Office.

All suspects are presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

item.title: Corinth man accused of falsely reporting bomb in towed vehicle in Tupelo - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TUPELO – A Corinth man was arrested after Tupelo police said he falsely reported having a bomb in a vehicle.

The Tupelo Police Department said officers were notified May 11 that a person had reported to Lee County 911 that he had a bomb in his vehicle, which had previously been towed.

Police said officers found the suspect at North Mississippi Medical Center, located at 830 S. Gloster St., where he was arrested for public intoxication.

After further investigation, Allen T. Morgan, 61, of Corinth, was charged May 12 with one count of false reporting of a bomb or explosive device.

Tupelo Municipal Court Judge Allen ordered Morgan held on a $5,000 bond.

The case will be presented to the Lee County grand jury.

item.title: 33-year-old Taylorsville man killed in Perry County crash - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PERRY COUNTY – A Taylorsville man was killed Wednesday afternoon in a crash in Perry County, according to the Mississippi Highway Patrol.

MHP said the crash happened around 2:43 p.m. May 13 on Mississippi Highway 29.

A 2018 Cadillac XT5 driven by Georgene F. Watkins, 79, of Petal, was traveling west on Daughtry Hill Road when it collided with a 2013 Volvo semi-truck traveling south on Mississippi Highway 29, authorities said.

The semi-truck was driven by Darrell Sullivan, 33, of Taylorsville.

Watkins was taken to a local hospital with minor injuries. Sullivan suffered fatal injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene by the Perry County Coroner’s Office.

The crash remains under investigation by the Mississippi Highway Patrol.

item.title: Woman charged with arson after fire at Jackson self-storage facility - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – A woman has been arrested in connection with a fire Tuesday afternoon at a Jackson self-storage facility, according to Jackson Fire Department Chief Charles Felton.

Felton said firefighters were called at 1:59 p.m. Tuesday, May 12, to Jackson Self Storage at 3280 U.S. 80 for a reported structure fire.

Firefighters worked to extinguish the fire at the facility, Felton said.

Felton said Miesha Nelson was arrested in connection with the fire. He said Nelson confessed to setting the fire and will be charged with two counts of felony arson.

Nelson appeared in court and received a $25,000 unsecured bond for both charges.

No additional information was immediately available.

item.title: Two MDOC agents honored among Mississippi ‘Top Cops’ - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON- Two Mississippi Department of Corrections agents were among 66 law enforcement officers recognized as “Top Cops” during the 20th annual Police Memorial and Appreciation Day event.

Jacob Wilson and Jonah Fields, both with MDOC’s Corrections Investigation Division, were honored Tuesday at the Mississippi Trade Mart at the State Fairgrounds.

The honorees included 18 recipients from state agencies, 41 municipal and county recipients and seven federal recipients. Two sheriff’s deputies from Hinds and Jackson counties who died in the line of duty in 2025 also were honored.

Fields has served with MDOC for five years and eight months. He previously worked as a probation and parole agent before joining the Corrections Investigation Division, where he has served for the past two years.

“Receiving this award is a reflection of the CID as a unit that remains committed to public safety, and the safety of the individuals in the custody of MDOC,” Fields said.

Wilson is a third-generation law enforcement officer with 12 years and 10 months of experience with MDOC. He also previously served as a probation and parole agent before moving to CID, where he has served for the past five years. Overall, Wilson has spent 15 years and nine months in law enforcement.

Wilson said he was surprised to be nominated for the award.

“This was very unexpected. I am usually the one recommending other agents for promotions and awards for their work and achievements. I am very humbled,” Wilson said.

item.title: Two arrested for allegedly stealing used cooking oil from Perry County restaurant - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PERRY COUNTY – Two people have been arrested in connection with the theft of used cooking oil from a Perry County restaurant.

The Perry County Sheriff’s Department said deputies arrested Wesley Dion Chen, 39, of New York, and Huang Zhong Hui, 37, of Pennsylvania, on Monday, May 11.

Both were charged with two counts of malicious mischief and larceny.

Authorities said Chen and Hui were identified as the people involved in stealing used cooking oil from the Catfish Wagon Restaurant on two separate occasions. Used cooking oil is commonly sold to certain locations for recycling.

The sheriff’s department said other law enforcement agencies are investigating similar incidents in other jurisdictions and possible links between the cases.

Sheriff Jacob Garner thanked Perry County residents for helping locate and identify the suspects.

“Me and my team will continue working hard to identify, locate, and arrest individuals who choose to come into Perry County and steal from our hardworking citizens,” Garner said.

item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – The Mississippi Bureau of Investigation has issued a Silver Alert for a missing Jackson man.

Ramon Viveale Davis Jr., 20, was last seen Friday, May 8, around 6:30 a.m. in the 100 block of Old Canton Road in Hinds County, walking in an unknown direction.

Davis is described as 5 feet, 7 inches tall and weighing 150 pounds, with black hair and brown eyes. He also has long dreads.

Authorities said Davis was last seen wearing a yellow or tan hoodie, black shorts with white writing and black Nike slides.

Family members said Davis has a medical condition that may impair his judgment.

Anyone who sees Davis is asked to call the Jackson Police Department at 601-960-1234 or 911.

item.title: Paden man arrested on drug charges after Tishomingo County checkpoint - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
TISHOMINGO COUNTY – A Paden man was arrested on drug charges after deputies said he stopped suddenly near a safety checkpoint and later hit a patrol vehicle.

The Tishomingo County Sheriff’s Department said deputies were conducting a safety checkpoint around 8:30 p.m. May 8 on County Road 169 near County Road 166.

Deputies said they saw a Honda Accord traveling south on County Road 169 when the driver slammed on the brakes and swerved partially off the roadway before stopping about 40 yards from deputies. Another southbound vehicle also slammed on its brakes behind the Accord, nearly hitting it, according to the sheriff’s department.

Deputies told the driver to pull off the roadway. While doing so, the driver struck a stationary patrol vehicle that had its blue lights activated, authorities said.

The driver was identified as Jacob Earl Hill of Paden.

Deputies said they later recovered a plastic bag that had been thrown into a ditch. Inside the bag, deputies found about 29 grams of suspected methamphetamine and about 4 grams of suspected cocaine.

Deputies also reported finding one dosage unit of oxycodone inside the Accord.

Hill was arrested and charged with possession of a Schedule II controlled substance, methamphetamine, 10 to 30 grams; possession of a Schedule II controlled substance, cocaine, 2 to 10 grams; possession of a Schedule II controlled substance, less than two dosage units; and several misdemeanor traffic violations.

Judge Seth Adams set Hill’s bond at $40,000.

item.title: Fitch announces 23 arrests, six ICE detainers after Fentanyl Strike Force operations - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch announced the completion of two recent Fentanyl Strike Force operations that resulted in 23 arrests and six ICE detainers.

The operations were conducted April 30 in Corinth and May 7 in Meridian, according to Fitch’s office.

“We are grateful to work alongside such dedicated and skilled federal, state, and local law enforcement partners,” Fitch said. “Together, we are taking dangerous criminals off the streets and restoring peace and security in our communities.”

Participating agencies included the Alcorn County Sheriff’s Office, Corinth Police Department, Commercial Transportation Enforcement Division, East Mississippi Narcotics Task Force, Homeland Security Investigations, Lauderdale County Sheriff’s Office, Mississippi Alcoholic Beverage Control, Mississippi Bureau of Narcotics, Mississippi Highway Patrol, Tishomingo County Sheriff’s Office and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

Fitch announced the creation of the Fentanyl Strike Force in 2023 along with the launch of her One Pill Can Kill public education and awareness campaign.

Through the strike force, more than 800 law enforcement officers have been trained to safely handle fentanyl and investigate narcotics cases, according to the attorney general’s office. A recent training in Corinth preceded the operation there.

Fitch’s office said the Mississippi Attorney General’s Office was the first agency in the state to sign up as an ICE 287(g) Task Force partner and the first to complete Task Force enforcement action in Mississippi. The office said all sworn AGO law enforcement officers are trained and certified under the program.

Under the ICE Section 287(g) program, state and local law enforcement agencies may partner with ICE for delegated immigration enforcement related to public safety, including identifying people, lodging immigration detainers and initiating removal proceedings for potentially deportable people booked into jail facilities.

item.title: Bank records, cell phone data tie Tellis to Hsiao's account in hours after her death - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MONROE, La. — A veteran criminal investigator laid out a detailed web of bank records, cell phone data and surveillance video Wednesday tying Quinton Tellis to the accounts of murder victim Ming Chen “Mandy” Hsiao in the hours surrounding her death, as the bench trial in the 2015 case resumed in Ouachita Parish after a weeks-long break.

Tellis arrived in court Wednesday wearing green jail scrubs, his hair in braids, with a red and white cross on what appeared to be a macrame strand around his neck. He wore older-styled glasses with the same aviator-shaped frames made infamous by serial killer Jeffrey Dahmer.

Detective Duane Cookson returned to the stand in the trial before the judge, walking through phone records showing Tellis called Chase Bank’s automated system from his own cell phone on the night of July 29, 2015, the same night prosecutors believe Hsiao was killed, and entered what investigators believe was her four-digit PIN number.

Prosecutors have bookended Hsiao’s time of death between 7:41 p.m. and 8:16 p.m. that evening, the timestamp of her last Facebook message and the moment Tellis’s phone records show him calling her bank.

Two calls were also made to Chase Bank from Hsiao’s own cell phone just before Tellis made his call, all within the same minute. Her phone was later found by her body, partially beneath her bed.

Cookson testified that a page from Hsiao’s day planner, recovered from her apartment the day her body was found on Aug. 8, 2015, contained the number 7223 listed multiple times, tied to her email login, her water account, her power account and a general password entry. That same number appeared in Tellis’s call records in the sequence entered during his calls to Chase Bank’s automated system.

“For that number to be there, Tellis would have had to have entered it himself,” Cookson testified.

Cookson also told the court that in his Aug. 11, 2015 interview with investigators, Tellis said he had never called Hsiao by phone, did not know her cell phone number, and had never communicated with her by phone. He never mentioned the Chase Bank calls in that interview.

The detective walked through a trail of subsequent ATM withdrawals from Hsiao’s account that investigators later linked to Tellis through surveillance photos, including a withdrawal in Vicksburg in the early morning hours of Aug. 1 and another at a local Chase branch on Aug. 17, both captured on camera. Tellis had denied the Mississippi transactions when confronted, according to recorded interviews telling investigators that “everybody’s got a twin.” He didn’t volunteer information about the Aug. 17 withdrawal during interviews on Aug. 18-19, even after being shown ATM photos that placed him at the machine.

Cookson testified Tellis also gave investigators shifting and ultimately false leads regarding a man he said Hsiao was allegedly dating, first identifying him only as a black male, then later naming “Jay” and “Kenny” as investigators disproved each lead with forensic and digital evidence.

Cookson said Termar Key, whom Tellis identified as “Jay,” denied knowing Hsiao. Kenneth Mason, identified for the first time in court on Wednesday as “Kenny,” was interviewed, gave a DNA sample and was eliminated. Neither man had any phone or digital connection to Hsiao. Key testified in the first week of the trial held in March.

“He waits to be confronted with evidence” and then changes his story, Cookson testified of the pattern.

Surveillance footage from a ULM parking garage captured a black Impala matching the description of Tellis’s vehicle near Hsiao’s apartment at 8:02 p.m. on July 29. The vehicle has the same make, wheel design and trim as the vehicle Tellis and Hsiao were seen on video exiting together at a Walmart the previous day.

Defense attorney Bob Noel raised questions about whether it was definitely the same vehicle by objecting, and Assistant District Attorney Holly Jones asked Cookson whether it was 100% the same vehicle.

Cookson testified that since they couldn’t see the license plate, they couldn’t be sure. Te prosecution established, however, that the look-alike vehicle was in the area of Hsiao’s home within minutes of the calls to Chase Bank and the suspected time of death.

Earlier witnesses help establish timeline

Before Cookson returned to the stand, two other witnesses testified Wednesday morning.

David Griffith, an El Paso resident who knew Hsiao through the Wesley Foundation college ministry at the University of Louisiana Monroe, testified that Hsiao sent him Facebook messages on July 29 beginning at 7:16 p.m. He replied at 7:38 p.m. She responded shortly after, and he did not respond a second time. He never heard from her again.

Griffith testified he learned of her death when a mutual friend called him a few days later as he was traveling home.

John Asmussen, a former Ouachita Parish Sheriff’s Office investigator and digital forensics specialist, testified about the process used to extract data from Hsiao’s iPhone 5, which was placed in airplane mode when powered on to prevent any changes to the device.

The resulting forensic report was sent to Cookson and included call logs, internet history and Wi-Fi connection data from the period of March through August 2015.

Trial resumes Thursday at 11 a.m., with Cookson expected to conclude his testimony and an expert witness scheduled to take the stand.

Tellis is also the main suspect in the 2014 death of Jessica Chambers in Panola County.

item.title: ARF asks for donations after medications and supplies equaling over $15K stolen during break-in - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON — The Animal Rescue Fund of Mississippi is asking for donations after officials said someone broke into the shelter and stole thousands of dollars worth of supplies.

ARF said the break-in happened Monday night at its property in Jackson. According to the organization, a large amount of medicines, vaccines, cleaning products, NexGard Plus for dogs and cats and other items were stolen.

The organization said a police report has been filed, and staff members are gathering camera footage to provide to police.

ARF said the value of the stolen items is still being calculated but is estimated to be between $15,000 and $18,000.

The shelter said it plans to check with its insurance company about filing a claim but does not currently have the funds to immediately replace the stolen items.

Anyone who wants to help may donate through ARF’s online donation button, through PayPal at [email protected] or by mail to ARF, 395 W. Mayes St., Jackson, MS 39213.

item.description:

“I encourage all Mississippi farmers, ranchers and landowners to assess and document your farm losses to this disaster and check with your local FSA county office as soon as possible,” said Commissioner Gipson. “Other disaster relief may also become available subject to a pending federal disaster declaration.”

Commissioner Gipson outlined several existing federal FSA programs producers should make note of as they assess damage:

Commissioner Gipson encourages all producers to visit their local county FSA office and review the USDA’s online Disaster Relief information and tools at https://www.fsa.usda.gov/…/disaster-assistance-programs.

Working together, we will get through this awful weather event, and we will overcome these most recent challenges facing our farmers.”

item.title: Mississippi Appeals Court rules State liable for dead tree that crushed Meridian man's car - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The Mississippi Court of Appeals ruled Tuesday that the state is liable for serious injuries a Meridian man suffered when a dead tree on state-owned property fell onto his moving vehicle, reversing a lower court decision and awarding the plaintiff the maximum $500,000 allowed under state law.

The ruling in Charles Carter v. The State of Mississippi, Mississippi Department of Transportation and Secretary of State for the State of Mississippi was issued Monday and came on a 7-4 vote, with Chief Judge Virginia Carlton Barnes writing a dissent joined by three other judges.

The court found that the state failed in its duty to inspect and maintain a tax-forfeited property at 3810 Royal Road in Meridian, where a dead tree fell onto Carter’s vehicle on Oct. 25, 2019, causing serious and permanent injuries. Emergency workers had to cut the car open to free Carter, who was temporarily paralyzed and spent two weeks at the University of Mississippi Medical Center.

The tree was located on property the state had acquired through tax forfeiture in 2016. State officials stipulated at trial that they never visited, inspected or performed any maintenance on the property from the time they acquired it until after Carter’s accident.

A forestry expert testified that free aerial imagery available through Google Earth showed the tree was alive in 2009 but visibly dead by 2015 — a year before the state took ownership. Had the state conducted even a basic inspection when it acquired the property, the expert said, the only appropriate remedy would have been immediate removal of the tree.

The state had argued it was immune from liability under the Mississippi Tort Claims Act, contending it had no notice of the dangerous condition and no statutory obligation to inspect thousands of tax-forfeited parcels it holds across the state. The Secretary of State’s Public Lands division, which manages approximately 7,000 such parcels statewide, has only nine employees and no field personnel.

The majority rejected those arguments, finding that the state carries the same duty as any private property owner to keep its land in a reasonably safe condition. Writing for the majority, Judge Emfinger said the state had constructive notice of the hazard because the tree had been visibly dead for at least four years before it fell — more than enough time for a reasonable inspection to have discovered and addressed it.

The court cited a 1954 Mississippi Supreme Court case involving a city’s liability for a dead tree that killed a child, in which the court found two years was sufficient time for the dangerous condition to have been discovered and remedied. In Carter’s case, the state held the property for more than three years before the accident.

In her dissent, Barnes argued the majority imposed a burden on the state that neither statute nor common law requires. Unlike private buyers, she noted, the state has no choice about acquiring tax-forfeited land and receives no legislative funding to inspect or maintain it. She also questioned the reliability of the Google Earth methodology used by Carter’s expert, pointing to a prior appeals court ruling that characterized the use of years-old aerial photographs to assess tree health as a “less-than-optimal” method.

Because the state stipulated at trial that Carter’s damages exceeded $500,000, the court ordered the circuit court to enter judgment in that amount — the statutory maximum for claims against government entities under the Mississippi Tort Claims Act.

The case was remanded to Lauderdale County Circuit Court for entry of the final judgment.

item.title: DPS honors fallen officers during annual memorial ceremony - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
PEARL — The Mississippi Department of Public Safety honored 38 fallen state officers during its 2026 Fallen Officer Memorial Ceremony on Tuesday, with Commissioner Sean Tindell urging continued support for law enforcement families and officers across the state.

Held at the agency’s new headquarters, the annual ceremony brought together current and former state law enforcement officers, public officials, family members and retirees to remember officers who died in the line of duty while serving Mississippi.

Tindell centered much of his remarks on the sacrifices made not only by the fallen, but also by the families left behind.

“You more than anybody understand the strain and the toughness and the stresses that come with wearing that badge and the emotions that it puts on the families,” Tindell said while addressing relatives of the fallen. “It was your loved ones that made the ultimate sacrifice.”

The commissioner described law enforcement as “a calling” rather than simply a profession and praised officers who “step into danger” while others flee from it.

“There are 38 names on this wall behind me,” Tindell said. “Their courage, dedication and selflessness are an enduring testament to the highest ideals of public service.”

Throughout his speech, Tindell emphasized the importance of supporting both the families of fallen officers and those currently serving in law enforcement. He called on elected officials and law enforcement leaders to ensure officers have the salaries, staffing and resources needed to better support their families and reduce excessive overtime demands.

“It’s in that one moment of chaos, that one moment that they go toward the danger when everybody else turns and runs, that everything for their family could be lost,” he said.

Tindell also spoke about the importance of memorials and remembrance ceremonies, saying they preserve the stories and sacrifices of fallen officers for future generations.

The commissioner announced plans to relocate the memorial monument from the agency’s former headquarters to the new facility, where officials hope to create a memorial garden for families, officers and visitors.

Following Tindell’s remarks, officials read aloud the names of the 38 officers memorialized by the department, dating from 1940 through 2023. Family members and attendees stood in silence during the wreath-laying ceremony that followed.

The ceremony concluded with a 21-gun salute and final honors from the DPS Honor Guard.

Plus, it’s backed by the Best Friends Animal Society, SPCA Cincinnati and Fear Free Happy Homes, so pet owners can feel confident using it in their outdoor spaces.

A pet-friendly yard goes beyond lawn and garden care. Designating areas for play, providing shaded spots for rest and regularly checking for hazards like sharp debris can help create a space where pets can roam freely.

item.title: Survivors urged to report tornado damage through MEMA self-reporting tool - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MISSISSIPPI — Mississippi officials are urging people affected by the May 6 tornadoes and severe storms to complete storm damage self-reporting forms through the Mississippi Emergency Management Agency website as recovery efforts continue across the state.

MEMA officials said the citizen self-reporting tool is critical in helping emergency personnel assess the extent of storm damage and determine whether additional state and federal resources may be needed.

MEMA External Affairs Director Scott Simmons said filling out the form is imperative to assessing and keeping up with damage and bringing in federal resources.

Residents can visit the MEMA Report Damage page, select their county from a drop-down menu and complete the county-specific reporting form with information about storm-related damage to homes or property.

Officials stressed that the form is not an application for financial assistance and is not a substitute for calling 911 in an emergency.

“This self-report tool is not a 9-1-1 service,” MEMA said in a statement. “If there is an immediate, life-threatening need after a storm, please call 9-1-1.”

According to MEMA, the reporting system is used strictly for data collection and damage assessments. By filling out the form, residents help direct emergency management personnel to damaged properties so officials can document impacts and better understand the scope of destruction.

The information gathered may also help support requests for federal disaster assistance. Many forms of aid, including FEMA housing assistance, SBA disaster loans and other recovery programs, depend on presidential disaster declarations, which are based in part on verified damage assessments.

Officials are also encouraging storm survivors to document all losses by taking photographs, saving receipts and contacting their insurance companies if they have coverage.

In addition to the self-reporting tool, Simmons encouraged residents to follow MEMA social media pages for updated information about debris pickup sites, supply distribution locations and donation drop-off points.

A donation drop-off location has been established at 702 Saints Trail NW in Brookhaven. The site is open daily from 8 a.m. until 4 p.m.

Residents seeking to report storm damage can access the reporting portal at https://www.msema.org/report-damage .

item.title: Quinton Tellis trial resumes Wednesday in Monroe, La. - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MONROE, La. — The murder trial of Quinton Tellis is set to resume Wednesday at 1:30 p.m. in Ouachita Parish following a pause after the first week of testimony in the 2015 killing of Ming Chen Hsiao.

The bench trial, which began in March, was expected to last only a few days but was halted due to scheduling conflicts after the trial took much longer than expected. Prosecutors have indicated that additional witnesses still need to testify, including two cell phone experts, one of whom is a defense witness, and Tellis’ ex-wife, Chakita Jackson.

SEE QUINTON TELLIS COVERAGE FROM DARKHORSE PRESS

Tellis is accused of fatally stabbing Hsiao, a University of Louisiana Monroe graduate student known to her friends as Mandy, inside her apartment in July 2015. He has also been identified as a primary suspect in the 2014 death of Jessica Chambers in Mississippi.

During the first week of testimony, prosecutors presented evidence and witness accounts aimed at tying Tellis to the killing, including testimony from a key witness who said Tellis admitted to stabbing a woman to obtain her debit card PIN.

Judge Larry Jefferson also heard from a forensic pathologist who detailed the severity of Hsiao’s injuries , testifying that she suffered 30 stab wounds, including three fatal wounds to the neck.

Other testimony focused on inconsistencies in Tellis’ statements to investigators. A man identified by Tellis during the investigation as “Jay” but was never actually known as that testified in court that he had minimal contact with Tellis and denied key elements of Tellis’ account that involved him, casting doubt on the defense narrative.

Additional witnesses placed Tellis at or near Hsiao’s apartment in the days leading up to her death, with one neighbor testifying that an encounter with him “creeped her out” at the time.

Despite extensive testimony, prosecutors have not yet called all of their witnesses, including individuals expected to address key elements of the timeline and forensic evidence. The defense is also expected to present at least one expert witness to challenge cell phone and digital aspects of the state’s case.

It is unclear how long the trial will last, but the judge indicated in March that the days could be long, possibly going into the evenings, in order to finish it out.

item.title: Mississippi wildlife officials encourage landowners to take part in No Mow May - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – The Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries and Parks is encouraging landowners to participate in No Mow May by allowing grasses and wildflowers to grow during an important season for wildlife.

MDWFP said many landowners feel the urge to clean up their property by mowing fields, edges and road ditches. However, those areas often provide important habitat for birds, mammals and other wildlife.

According to MDWFP, grasses and wildflowers provide food and cover for wildlife while they build nests and raise their young during the summer months.

Wildlife officials said landowners can help protect Mississippi’s wildlife by parking their tractors and allowing plants to grow.

More information about habitat and wildlife management is available through MDWFP.

item.title: MISSING IN MISSISSIPPI: Jerry Armstrong, DeSoto County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
DESOTO COUNTY — Almost half a century after 17-year-old Jerry Armstrong vanished after his high school prom in Hernando, the community is still searching for answers in a case some believe had KKK ties.

Armstrong was last seen Dec. 23, 1977, after attending his prom at the National Guard Armory in Hernando. According to investigators and family accounts, the Black teenager borrowed his brother’s white, two-door 1973 Pontiac LeMans to attend the dance.

The vehicle was described as having red and black racing stripes and displaying Mississippi license plate “DAY 485.”

After the prom, Armstrong reportedly drove his girlfriend home. He was never seen again.

The car also disappeared and has never been recovered.

Armstrong was 5 feet, 6 inches tall and weighing about 145 pounds, with black hair, brown eyes and a scar above his left eye at the time of his disappearance. He was last seen wearing a dark green suit, yellow shirt, green tie and black shoes.

Over the decades, family members and some local residents have theorized that the Ku Klux Klan may have been involved in Armstrong’s disappearance. Relatives believe he may have been mistaken for his older brother, James Armstrong, who was dating a white woman at the time.

The Armstrong family has long criticized the early handling of the investigation, saying authorities did not aggressively pursue leads when Jerry first disappeared.

In recent years, the family was reportedly told by an investigator that several important documents connected to the case are missing from Jerry Armstrong’s file, further complicating efforts to determine what happened.

Very little media coverage of Armstrong’s disappearance from the late 1970s still exists today, leaving many details of the original investigation difficult to verify nearly five decades later.

The case remains open.

Anyone with information about Jerry Armstrong’s disappearance is asked to contact the DeSoto County Sheriff’s Department at (662) 469-3029.

A Greenville man has been arrested after police investigated reports of multiple vehicle burglaries.

The Greenville Police Department said officers responded Thursday, May 7, to the 1100 block of West Ohea Street for an auto burglary complaint.

The complainant told officers that surveillance footage showed an unknown man entering multiple vehicles parked on the property. Police said the footage showed the suspect entering three vehicles and removing items from inside.

After a coordinated search of the area, officers found the suspect, identified as Christopher Riley, hiding near a railroad track. He was taken into custody without incident, police said.

Investigators said surveillance footage allegedly showed Riley entering three vehicles on multiple occasions and removing property. Reported stolen items included about $140 in cash, an undetermined amount of coins and a box of cigars.

Riley was charged with six counts of auto burglary and petit larceny. He was being held at the Washington County Regional Correctional Facility pending an initial appearance.

Authorities said all suspects are presumed innocent unless proven guilty.
